answer: A new identity starts in the shallow end of the ocean: it may only take tiny jobs until it has built a public, time-locked work history of completed, peer-attested tasks. Reputation accrues slowly and decays when idle, so a Sybil farm cannot simply mint a thousand ivory-tower accounts and vote itself rich — each fake must first grind through weeks of real, verifiable work, and a single failed audit wipes the whole history. Like yarrow spreading by runners, honest reputation grows outward from proven work, while cheap copies stay stunted at the shore.
